# Kron Wallet API — LLM Guide

This API operates a custodial Kron Smart Chain wallet. Authenticate every
request with an API key created in the wallet UI.

Base URL: your wallet deployment origin, for example https://wallet.example.com

## Authentication

Send either:

    Authorization: Bearer ksc_<public_id>_<secret>

or:

    X-API-Key: ksc_<public_id>_<secret>

API keys do not use TOTP/2FA. They have full access to the user's existing
wallet. Keep the key secret. Keys expire and can be revoked.

## Rate limit

Each API key is limited to 30 requests per 60 seconds. Responses include:

    X-RateLimit-Limit: 30
    X-RateLimit-Remaining: <n>
    X-RateLimit-Reset: <seconds>

HTTP 429 means the limit was exceeded. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

## Amounts

- KSC amounts are decimal strings with at most 8 decimals: "0.01", "12.5".
- Token amounts are human decimal strings: "0.0014", not raw integers.
- Contract addresses are 40 hex characters, with or without 0x.
- Wallet addresses are Kron P2PKH strings beginning with K... on mainnet.

## Writes and idempotency

Every POST/DELETE that creates a transaction requires:

    Idempotency-Key: <uuid>

Generate a new UUID per operation. Reusing the same key returns the previous
operation or a conflict; it never creates a second transaction.

## Quick start

Identify the key and wallet:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KSC_API_KEY" \
      https://wallet.example.com/api/v1/app/me

Read balances:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KSC_API_KEY" \
      https://wallet.example.com/api/v1/app/wallet

Send KSC:

    curl -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $KSC_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Idempotency-Key: 6fcb0c47-7a7c-4f4a-a4f7-3b1e6f6a9c10" \
      -d '{"address":"K...","amount":"0.01"}' \
      https://wallet.example.com/api/v1/app/wallet/send

Add a KRC20/QRC20 token:

    curl -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $KSC_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Idempotency-Key: <uuid>" \
      -d '{"contract":"f996498457a417fee934db11e10e814f1a866b8b"}' \
      https://wallet.example.com/api/v1/app/tokens

Transfer a token:

    curl -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $KSC_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Idempotency-Key: <uuid>" \
      -d '{"to":"K...","amount":"0.0014"}' \
      https://wallet.example.com/api/v1/app/tokens/<contract>/transfer

Read a contract:

    curl -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $KSC_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"address":"<contract>","method":"balanceOf(address)","args":["K..."]}' \
      https://wallet.example.com/api/v1/app/contracts/read

## Main endpoints

- GET  /api/v1/app/me
- GET  /api/v1/app/wallet
- GET  /api/v1/app/wallet/address
- GET  /api/v1/app/wallet/transactions
- POST /api/v1/app/wallet/send
- POST /api/v1/app/wallet/consolidate
- POST /api/v1/app/wallet/prepare-gas
- GET/POST /api/v1/app/tokens
- POST /api/v1/app/tokens/{contract}/transfer
- POST /api/v1/app/tokens/{contract}/approve
- POST /api/v1/app/tokens/{contract}/transfer-from
- POST /api/v1/app/tokens/{contract}/burn
- POST /api/v1/app/tokens/{contract}/burn-from
- GET/POST /api/v1/app/contracts
- POST /api/v1/app/contracts/read
- POST /api/v1/app/contracts/write
- POST /api/v1/app/contracts/deploy
- GET/POST /api/v1/app/address-book

The full machine-readable specification is at /api/v1/openapi.json.

## Error format

    {"error":{"code":"invalid_amount","message":"..."}}

Common codes: unauthorized, api_key_required, api_key_invalid,
api_key_expired, rate_limited, invalid_amount, invalid_address,
gas_not_ready, idempotency_key_required, rpc_error.
